name: stalled-reader
notes: A reader process is SIGSTOPed while its socket is ESTABLISHED and carries unread data in the receive queue.
Tier B counters (bytes acked/received) advance until the stop, then freeze past the 30s stall threshold: NETWORK_PROGRESS_STOPPED is observed, not fabricated.
PROCESS_STOP_CAUSES_NETWORK_PROGRESS_LOSS@1 links the stop to the stall: the owner binds to the stopped incarnation and recv_q is non-zero.
The stop event carries the LOCAL_NOT_READING stamp (§7.2): the receive queue is observed non-empty while the Tier B counters are frozen, so receipt fails, not broker receipt or path failure.

The open stall is itself anchored (§7.3): its analysis stays UNKNOWN with an UNEXPLAINED_HEAD candidate — the stop explains the stall but the cause of the stop is not captured — and its alternatives cite the shape discriminators: LOCAL_NOT_READING reverses the arrow, broker and path hypotheses are abandoned for the LOCAL_NOT_READING shape.

missing_evidence_includes: stop-sender telemetry (who sent SIGSTOP/ptrace) is not captured in v1 bundles
job/application progress over the stalled socket is not observed in v1 (WORKER_PROGRESS_STOPPED), and Tier C blocked-in-read evidence is not captured
alternatives: network stall shape LOCAL_NOT_READING points at the local process not reading: the stall is an effect of a local stop, not a broker or path failure
